nodes.title: Scalar maps on locally free arithmetic classes
nodes.statement: For a compatible homomorphism of arithmetic orders Λ→Γ, extension takes locally free rank-n Λ-lattices to locally free rank-n Γ-lattices and induces Cl(Λ)→Cl(Γ), whenever coefficient completions commute with this scalar change. If Γ itself is a locally free Λ-lattice of fixed rank d, restriction induces Cl(Γ)→Cl(Λ). On a rank-n Γ-lattice P its formula is Res(cΓ(P))=cΛ(Res P)−n·cΛ(Res Γ), with Res P of local rank nd. In particular it equals cΛ(Res P) only when the coefficient-order correction class vanishes. Merely being an overorder does not imply the restriction hypothesis.
proofSteps: Use the balanced universal property to commute extension with central coefficient completions, then compute on completed free bases. For restriction use Γ_v≅Λ_vᵈ. The defining class [P]−n[Γ] restricts to [Res P]−n[Res Γ]; add and subtract nd[Λ] to obtain cΛ(Res P)−n cΛ(Res Γ). For Z[G]→O_F[G], an integral Z-basis of O_F makes Res Γ globally free of rank [F:Q], so the correction class is zero.

nodes.title: Steinitz decomposition over a Dedekind domain
nodes.statement: A nonzero finitely generated torsion-free module M over a Dedekind domain A of fraction-field rank n is isomorphic to Aⁿ⁻¹⊕I for a nonzero invertible fractional ideal I. Two such modules are isomorphic iff their ranks and ideal classes agree. The rank-zero case is M=0. Fields are handled separately by a vector-space basis.
proofSteps: Embed M in K⊗M. Choose a nonzero coordinate projection; its image is a fractional ideal. Invertibility supplies a dual basis and hence projectivity of that image, so the projection splits. Induct on rank to decompose M into ideals. Apply steinitz-ideal-product repeatedly. For uniqueness use the top exterior power and the existing principal-scaling class criterion.

nodes.title: The norm of a projective group-ring module reaches all invariants
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring A, finite group G and projective left A[G]-module P, the group norm induces an A-linear isomorphism P_G→P^G from coinvariants to invariants. In particular every invariant m is ∑g∈G gx for some x∈P. Restriction to a subgroup preserves projectivity and the same statement. For a Galois integral lattice the norm is the field trace.
proofSteps: For A[G], coinvariants are A by augmentation, and invariants are A times the group norm; the induced norm sends 1 to that basis element, so it is an isomorphism. Extend to arbitrary free modules and then transport the isomorphism to a projective retract, since norm commutes with the splitting maps. Restriction to H preserves projectivity because A[G] is free over A[H]. Identify the Galois norm with the sum defining the integral trace.

nodes.title: Ideles and lattice gluing for an arithmetic order
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional semisimple algebra B over a number field F, an O_F-order Λ and each finite place v, put B_v=F_v⊗B and Λ_v=O_v⊗Λ. For α∈J(B), I(α)=B∩∏finite-v α_vΛ_v is a full right Λ-lattice with those completions. Left Λ-modules are obtained by applying this construction to Bᵒᵖ,Λᵒᵖ. All ensuing idele formulae use this opposite-algebra convention.

nodes.title: Local and global reduced-norm images
nodes.statement: For each central simple number-field component C/F, Nrd(C×) consists exactly of a∈F× positive at every real place where C_v is a matrix algebra over Hamilton quaternions. At finite v the image is all F_v×; for a maximal O_v-order its unit image is O_v×. At a ramified real place it is ℝ_{>0}, otherwise the full local centre group. For any finite-place order, its norm-unit image is open. These statements apply componentwise to semisimple B.
proofSteps: Reduce each local simple component to M_r(D). Import the local Brauer invariant and its restriction formula: a degree-d extension kills the invariant of a division algebra D of degree d. The splitting/embedding criterion then embeds both the unramified degree-d extension and a degree-d totally ramified Eisenstein extension as maximal subfields. Their integral rings lie in the unique maximal order of D. Import unramified unit-norm surjectivity from LocalFieldsRamification Layer2 and the norm valuation formula from Layer3: the first supplies every unit and a uniformizer of the second supplies valuation one. Morita invariance and conjugacy of maximal orders give the asserted matrix-order unit image. At infinity compute split-real, complex and quaternionic determinants. For the global step, choose local regular elements with prescribed norm, approximate their separable reduced characteristic polynomials while fixing the constant term, and use prescribed-separable-polynomial to realize that polynomial globally. Split places supply companion matrices. This is Kneser’s §5.4 proof using the global Brauer splitting criterion. Openness follows from the reduced trace on sufficiently deep principal units.

nodes.title: Inner forms meet the strong-approximation hypotheses
nodes.statement: For a central simple C/F of degree d>1, SL₁(C) is connected semisimple and simply connected. The inner-form identification is PRR Proposition2.37: a splitting trivialization gives an inner cocycle in PGL_d and descent of the determinant-one equations. Geometric connectedness and simple connectedness are preserved by this form. Explicit diagonal one-parameter subgroups prove noncompactness in all allowed real or complex matrix cases.

nodes.title: Stable idele classification in every semisimple case
nodes.statement: For an arithmetic order Λ in semisimple B, its locally free stable class group is J(B)/(J(B)′ B× U(Λ)). For each m≥2, locally free rank-m lattices are classified by this quotient via their GL_m(B) adelic basis matrices and reduced norms. No decomposition into rank-one ideals is assumed in constructing this classification. No Eichler hypothesis on B is needed. The quotient is abelian and identifies with inherited Cl(Λ) inside projective K₀.

Since M_m(B) satisfies Eichler for m≥2, strong approximation removes its norm-one fibre. The stable equality theorem identifies equal stable classes in SplitK0 with these stabilized isomorphisms. To ensure no loss from the ambient projective K₀ use a finite free complement of every projective stabilization witness.

nodes.statement: Let C/F be central simple of degree d and f∈F[X] monic separable of degree d. Elementary matrices have determinant one in every splitting representation; multiply the diagonal unit determinants.

nodes.title: Positive unit homomorphisms and the kernel group
nodes.statement: Let Hom_Ω⁺(R_G,U(Q̄)) mean the homomorphisms whose value on every virtual symplectic character is a positive real number at every archimedean component, including complex places. Set D_H=Hom_Ω⁺(R_G,U(Q̄))/(Hom_Ω⁺(R_G,O_Q̄×)·Det U(ℤ[G])). For S={p:p divides |G|}, this also has the finite-place presentation Hom_Ω(R_G,U_S)/(Hom_Ω⁺(R_G,O_Q̄×)·Det(ℤ_S[G]×)). Positivity remains in the principal denominator; the finite numerator has no archimedean component.
proofSteps: Use ramified-real norm positivity to identify maximal-order determinant units with positive unit homomorphisms. Intersect the principal denominator with unit ideles: this gives algebraic units, with positive values on symplectic characters. Eliminate the infinite components and the finite places outside S by weak approximation and maximality there, retaining positivity in the diagonal algebraic-unit denominator.

nodes.title: Absolute and relative norm resolvents
nodes.statement: For a G-Galois number-field extension L/F and normal generator a, form r_G(a)=∑g∈G g(a)g⁻¹∈L[G]× and (a|χ)=Det(r_G(a))(χ). For absolute ℤ[G] classes apply the character-hom norm N_F/ℚ: (N f)(χ)=∏ω f(χ^{ω⁻¹})^ω, over a right transversal of Ω_F in Ω_ℚ. Use the same construction on semilocal integral generators a_v and take their ratio against a rational normal generator. The absolute integer-ring rank is [F:ℚ], not one unless F=ℚ.
proofSteps: Normal-basis invertibility supplies the resolvent unit. Representation determinants supply character additivity and the twisted Galois rule. Norming the homomorphism over embeddings makes the absolute representative; a transversal change differs by a group determinant, so only its quotient class is canonical. The ratio of local and rational norm resolvents is the adelic basis matrix determinant.

nodes.title: Normal bases and invertible resolvents
nodes.statement: For a finite G-Galois algebra E/F and a∈E, the F[G]-map sending g to g(a) is bijective iff r_G(a)=Σg g(a)g⁻¹ is a unit in E[G]. Over a DVR, an integral resolvent is a unit in O_E[G] iff the integral algebra is étale and a is an integral normal-basis generator; this integral-unit criterion is not asserted for ramified tame extensions.
proofSteps: After scalar extension to a splitting field the regular multiplication matrix of the resolvent is the normal-basis conjugate matrix up to row and column permutations. A nonzero determinant is exactly bijectivity over the field. Over the integral ring invertibility is equivalent to a unit determinant, which is the discriminant criterion for the basis and étaleness.

nodes.title: Stickelberger’s finite Gauss-sum valuation
nodes.statement: Let q=pᶠ, P be a prime above p in Q(ζ_p,ζ_(q−1)), ω the Teichmüller character for its residue F_q, and ψ(x)=ζ_p^Tr(x). If 0≤a<q−1 has digits a_i, put s=Σa_i and h=∏a_i!. Then h·(−gaussSum(ω⁻ᵃ,ψ))≡(ζ_p−1)ˢ mod Pˢ⁺¹. Thus v_P(gaussSum)=s when v_P(ζ_p−1)=1, and the valuation with v_p(p)=1 is s/(p−1). The trivial-character case a=0 has valuation zero.
proofSteps: Expand normalized Jacobi sums modulo P using finite-field power sums; only the congruent exponents survive. Comparing coefficients in (1+ΣX_i)^m in characteristic p gives the digitwise multinomial congruence. Prove the a=1 base case directly: expand ζ_p^Tr(x) modulo (ζ_p−1)² and use Σx≠0 x⁻¹Tr(x)=−1 in F_q; this replaces Conrad’s unread Washington reference. Apply the two-Gauss double-sum identity to Jacobi sums, induct through the one-digit exponents, and use invariance under Frobenius to assemble the digits. The leading factorial is a unit, so the congruence gives the exact valuation.

Then h·(−gaussSum(ω⁻ᵃ,ψ))≡(ζ_p−1)ˢ mod Pˢ⁺¹. Thus v_P(gaussSum)=s when v_P(ζ_p−1)=1, and the valuation with v_p(p)=1 is s/(p−1). The trivial-character case a=0 has valuation zero.

nodes.title: The Hasse–Davenport product relation
nodes.statement: For F_q, a nontrivial additive character ψ, n≥1 dividing q−1, a multiplicative character λ of exact order n and any multiplicative χ (all extended by zero at zero), write g(θ)=gaussSum(θ,ψ). Then g(χⁿ)·∏_(j=1)^(n−1)g(λʲ)=χ(n)ⁿ·∏_(j=0)^(n−1)g(χλʲ). The trivial multiplicative character has g(1)=−1, so including j=0 in the left product changes the sign.
proofSteps: Reduce ψ to the trace-normalized additive character by the pinned scaling formula. Compare valuations and leading residues by finite-gauss-valuation and digit-factorial multiplication. The ratio has unit valuations and all complex conjugates of absolute value one, hence is a root of unity. Its leading residue fixes its prime-to-p part. The remaining p-power root-of-unity ambiguity must also be removed: this is the exact unread proof boundary G-DH, not an inference from valuations alone.

nodes.title: Tame local Galois Gauss sums
nodes.statement: Fix a finite extension F/Q_p, ψ_F=exp(2πi·Tr_F/Q_p(−)) with the usual rational p-adic additive character, and the local Artin convention of ClassFieldTheory. For a ramified one-dimensional finite-order character χ of conductor ideal fχ choose c generating D_F/Q_p·fχ and set τ_F(χ)=Σ_(u∈(O_F/fχ)×) χ(Art_F(u/c))ψ_F(u/c). For unramified χ set τ_F(χ)=χ(D_F/Q_p)⁻¹. Extend multiplicatively to virtual characters using the local-constant induction rule with its degree correction, and form the global finite product τ(χ). Independence and existence of this extension require G-LOCALCONSTANTS.
proofSteps: For degree one the conductor determines a finite sum independent of lifts; a change of generator is cancelled by character and additive-character reindexing. Import local Artin and conductor carriers. To extend beyond degree one use Brauer induction and the local-constant induction factor, checking all relations rather than choosing a Brauer expression arbitrarily. The unread relation/induction proof is explicitly G-LOCALCONSTANTS.

This equals the Artin functional-equation root factor by F76 (2.4)–(2.5). Define W_G on irreducibles to be this value on symplectic irreducibles and 1 on all others, and extend multiplicatively to R_G.
proofSteps: Import the Frobenius–Schur classification, local conductors and conjugation eigenspaces. The inverse Gauss formula fixes the convention without a complex-conjugation guess. The local/global symplectic duality identities give signs and tame Galois invariance via symplectic-root-sign-law. Comparison with analytic Artin functional equations is the explicit G-ARTIN boundary; the algebraic definition does not depend on having formalized Artin L-functions.

nodes.title: The integral group logarithm
nodes.statement: Let p be prime, R a characteristic-zero integral domain, p-torsion-free and p-adically complete, with an endomorphism F satisfying F(r)≡rᵖ mod pR. Let G be a finite p-group, I the augmentation ideal of R[G], C_G its conjugacy classes and φ:R[G]→R[C_G] the additive class projection. Set Ψ(r[g])=F(r)[gᵖ] on the class module and L(1+x)=(p−Ψ)φ(log(1+x)), x∈I. The logarithm converges in Frac(R)[G] because I mod p is nilpotent. Ψ is semilinear on the class module; it is not a ring homomorphism on a nonabelian group ring. Use ν=p⁻¹L on determinant classes where integrality permits.
proofSteps: Augmentation nilpotence modulo p gives I^N⊆pR[G], hence logarithmic convergence in R[1/p][G]. Project to conjugacy classes so logarithms are additive on products. Frobenius cancels denominators by group-log-integrality. For coefficientwise F_R on R[G], the exact character formula is χ(L(u))=p·log Det(u)(χ)−log Det(F_R(u))(ψᵖχ). F_R acts on coefficients before character evaluation; no extension of F_R fixing character roots is assumed. CPT denotes the map induced by L itself by ν; our normalized ν=L/p has image φ(A), while CPT’s ν has image pφ(A).

nodes.title: Taylor’s congruences detect the residual determinant torsion
nodes.statement: For the crossed-product Gauss factor f in gauss-log-image, let z and T′ be its commutator and abelian lifts. The quotient f/Det(zT′) lies in Det(G). Taylor’s four integral congruence families force this quotient to be trivial: induced characters of degree greater than two; degree-two characters with semiabelian action; degree-two inversion action; and degree-two semidihedral action. The Galois action permutes primes and induces the residue isomorphisms; the imported Dedekind prime-action dictionary supplies that normality.

nodes.title: Central flat scalar change for finite-order Hom modules

The canonical map S⊗ₐHom_Λ(M,N)→Hom_(S⊗ₐΛ)(S⊗ₐM,S⊗ₐN) is an isomorphism, compatible with composition and pure tensors. If S is faithfully flat, projectivity of S⊗M descends to M. A projective scalar extension makes Hom out of it preserve every surjection. Faithful flatness or joint detection reflects surjectivity of the Hom map, proving projectivity. nodes.title: One trace-dual lattice bounds every overorder
nodes.statement: Let A be integrally closed noetherian with fraction field F, B finite-dimensional with nondegenerate regular trace pairing, and Λ an A-order. Choose an F-basis e_i inside Λ and r=det(Tr_reg(e_ie_j))≠0. Every overorder Γ⊇Λ is contained in r⁻¹Σ_i A e_i. The bound is independent of Γ; it makes the set of overorders satisfy the ascending-chain condition.
proofSteps: Every x∈Γ is integral over A by finite-module Cayley–Hamilton. Eigenvalues of left multiplication are roots of a monic integral polynomial; their sum is integral over A and lies in F, hence regular trace lies in A by normality. Apply this to xe_j, since e_j∈Λ⊆Γ. Cramer’s rule in the fixed Gram matrix puts every coordinate in r⁻¹A. A noetherian finite-module bound gives ascending-chain termination.

nodes.title: Integral composita under arithmetic disjointness

nodes.title: A single tame cyclotomic conductor cut
nodes.statement: Suppose L⊆Q(ζ_m) and L/Q is Galois and tame. For odd pᵃ∥m, wild p-inertia in Gal(Q(ζ_m)/Q) acts trivially on L, so L⊆Q(ζ_(m/pᵃ·p)).
